conventions.convention: The autonomous scheme uses h=T/N≤1, Euclidean state norms, Frobenius matrix norms, left-endpoint coefficients, bar Y_T=Y_N, and continuous interpolation agreeing with the recursion at every grid point.
AC is assumed. The stochastic setup is complete and usual, and Brownian increments after s are independent of the full current filtration F_s.

The autonomous strong-rate contract assumes uniform path-supremum moments of every finite order for the exact, continuous Euler, and step processes. These are premises, not consequences of square-integrable initial data.

The finite-L² strong route requires global state Lipschitz bounds, uniform linear growth, a half-Hölder time modulus, and an initial value independent of future Brownian increments with finite second moment.

Weak order one is conditional on a bounded Borel payoff, the backward equation and terminal condition, continuous mixed derivatives through two time and four space derivatives bounded by C(1+|x|^q), and uniform pointwise p-moments with p≥2q+8. For q=0, |x|^q=1.

The refinement factor M≥2 is fixed; h≤1/M; both grids divide T; fine and coarse paths share the initial value and Brownian path; each coarse increment sums M fine increments. Work O(h⁻¹) assumes fixed dimensions and unit-cost coefficient and payoff evaluations.

load_bearing.statement: Under the stated complete usual filtered Brownian setup, global state-Lipschitz, linear-growth and half-Hölder time hypotheses, square-integrable initial data independent of future Brownian increments, and the exact solution's finite supremum second moment, E sup_{0≤t≤T}|X_t−Y_t^h|²≤Ch, uniformly over 0<h≤1 with T/h integral.

Under the stated Euler coefficient and Brownian hypotheses, bounded Borel payoff, backward equation and terminal condition, polynomially bounded continuous mixed derivatives through two time and four space derivatives, and uniform pointwise p-moments with p≥2q+8, |Eφ(X_T)−Eφ(Y_N^h)|≤Ch.

Under the finite-L² strong contract and the stated shared-Brownian nested-grid coupling, E|Y_T^h−Y_T^{Mh}|²≤C_Mh, Var(φ(Y_T^h)−φ(Y_T^{Mh}))≤C_M L_φ²h, and the payoff bias is at most C L_φ h^{1/2}. The additional bounded-payoff backward contract improves the bias to Ch. Under the stated cost assumptions, coupled sample work is O(h⁻¹).

For a predictable finite-energy row-vector integrand H against an m-dimensional Brownian motion in the stated complete usual filtered setup, E sup_{0≤t≤T}|Σ_j ∫₀ᵗ H_s^j dW_s^j|≤16√m E(∫₀ᵀ||H_s||₂² ds)^{1/2}.

Under the stated autonomous C¹, one-sided-Lipschitz drift, globally Lipschitz diffusion, polynomial local-Lipschitz drift and uniform all-moment premises, every even integer r≥2 satisfies sup_{0≤t≤T}E|Y_t^h−bar Y_t^h|^r≤C_r h^{r/2}, with C_r independent of h.

Under the stated autonomous C¹ coefficient inequalities and uniform path-supremum moments of every finite order for the exact, continuous Euler and step processes, E sup_{0≤t≤T}|X_t−Y_t^h|²≤Ch, with C independent of h.

Construct Y₀=X₀ and Y_{k+1}=Y_k+h f(Y_k)+g(Y_k)(W_{t_{k+1}}−W_{t_k}); return the grid recursion, left-endpoint step process with bar Y_T=Y_N, and continuous interpolation Y_t=Y_k+(t−t_k)f(Y_k)+g(Y_k)(W_t−W_{t_k}) on each grid interval.

concerns.concern: Proof step 2.1 says that on {M*>2λ, Q_T^{1/2}≤δλ}, 'the threshold defining σ is not reached before T'. The non-strict inequality permits the accumulated energy after τ to reach δ²λ² before T and then remain constant. Thus the quoted assertion does not follow as written. The good-lambda argument needs to address this equality case, for example by justifying that the integral cannot subsequently move when its remaining energy is zero. The maximal inequality itself is not contradicted.

seams_checked.note: Compared the algorithm, interpolation definition and uniform moment theorem with the finite-L² and weak-rate consumers. The consumers retain the state-Lipschitz, growth, time-modulus, mesh and initial-moment hypotheses. Pointwise moment bounds are not promoted to Euler path-supremum moment bounds; the strong proof obtains its error bound separately by stopping and Doob estimates.

Read both Euler MLMC corollaries against the autonomous strong theorem and shared-level/weak interfaces. The autonomous branch retains its all-moment premise. The finite-L² branch uses nested shared Brownian increments and retains the additional bounded-payoff backward regularity and p≥2q+8 requirements for the weak upgrade. T≤1 makes all geometric levels admissible, and the corollaries explicitly handle level-zero variance and work.
